finding: Condition 5 is specified as RolesStale's comparison "without its empty-stored-hash exemption", and the reason given is normative: "an empty stored hash means tp does not know which panel that round used, and a streak measured under an unknown panel must not produce the signal". Plain inequality does not implement that sentence. When the latest recorded round's stored roles_hash is empty AND the corpus hash computed now is also empty, the two compare equal, condition 5 is satisfied, and divergence fires over exactly the unknown panel the rationale forbids. The state is reachable and §2.1 names it: a round recorded while a role file could not be read, because ComputeRolesHash returns an empty string with an error that both audit callers discard. On --record §2.4 further states the condition is "satisfied by construction" because both values come from one computation in one invocation — so on that path an unreadable role file makes condition 5 unable to withhold the signal at all. A QA engineer cannot write a deterministic test for a both-empty fixture: the normative sentence says divergence must be absent, the stated comparison says it is present, and no §6 test resolves it (test 13 edits the corpus, so the current hash is non-empty there).

resolved.evidence: Addressed in the round-10 spec revision. Four roles independently found the same hole and it was real: an empty roles_hash is tp saying it could not read the corpus, but both SS2.1 cause 4 and SS2.4 condition 5 compared hashes as strings, so two empties compared equal and the signal fired -- or the walk continued -- under a panel tp cannot name. ComputeRolesHash returns an empty string with an error both audit callers discard, so a role file left unreadable across several records stamps the same empty value on all of them. An empty hash is now incomparable rather than a value: cause 4 ends the walk at any round whose stored hash is empty (including the latest round, through its own hash), and condition 5 requires both the stored and the freshly computed hash to be non-empty as well as equal, which is also what makes the --record path's satisfied-by-construction claim true only for the equality term. New tests 12's second half, 13 and 15 pin exactly those states. SS3.1 now exempts over-specification from mechanization entirely: tp appends a canonical-class instruction telling every reviewer to raise it, so putting it on the do-not-report list would ship one prompt that both demands and forbids the same finding; the check still runs and still gates --status --check, and test 34 pins the exclusion-list half as discriminating. Test 41's void assertion is replaced -- mechanical_checks is omitted under omitempty whether the runner returned nothing or was never called, so the skip notice is the assertion that can fail, and it is asserted per site. SS3.2 states the boundary of the failing-check safety property (a project-config check with no task file mechanizes without ever running), corrects the review_loop addendum claim (panel path only), and SS2.4 reattributes the other_roles_open guarantee to condition 1 for every threshold above zero. SS1 no longer claims an unchanged spec across the streak; Non-Goal 9 names the --report residual; SS6.1 is retitled and says plainly that nothing is invalidated.

finding: Condition 5 is specified as RolesStale's comparison 'without its empty-stored-hash exemption', justified by 'an empty stored hash means tp does not know which panel that round used, and a streak measured under an unknown panel must not produce the signal'. Dropping the exemption only changes the case where the stored hash is empty and the current hash is not; it does not cover the provenance §2.1 itself names. ComputeRolesHash returns "" with an error that both audit callers discard (internal/engine/rolehash.go:61, internal/cli/audit_record.go:106 and :187), so a round recorded while a role file was unreadable stores "", and if the file is still unreadable at report time the current hash is "" too — "" equals "", condition 5 is satisfied, and divergence fires under a panel tp cannot identify. On --record it is stronger than a hole: §2.4 makes condition 5 'satisfied by construction' by reading the stamped value back off the just-recorded round instead of hashing again, so the comparison is a tautology and the empty-hash state can never withhold the signal on that path at all. This is the direction §1 forbids ('a state tp cannot measure never produces the signal'), and the implementer must guess whether to add a non-emptiness term the stated rule does not contain.

finding: Condition 5's rule and its own rationale contradict each other in the one state the rationale is written for. The rule is plain equality between the latest round's stored `roles_hash` and the corpus hash computed now; the rationale is "an empty stored hash means tp does not know which panel that round used, and a streak measured under an unknown panel must not produce the signal". But an empty hash is produced by exactly one cause — `engine.ComputeRolesHash` returns "" only when a `.tp/auditors/*.json` file cannot be read (rolehash.go:61), and both audit callers discard that error (audit_record.go:106 and :187). If the same file is still unreadable when `--status` runs, stored "" equals current "" and condition 5 PASSES, so `divergence` fires under a panel tp cannot identify. On `--record` it is worse: §2.4 states the condition is "satisfied by construction" because the stamped value and the computed one come from one computation, which holds even when that one computation returned "" — so an empty stamped hash never withholds the signal there at all. §1's constraint ("a state tp cannot measure never produces the signal") is violated in both, and the spec never says what condition 5 does when the current hash is empty, so an implementer can satisfy the letter and break the intent.

finding: §3.1 makes per-entry validity the sole predicate for mechanization, and §3.2 leans on the safety property 'A failing check is already reported in mechanical_checks and already gates the exit code of tp review --status --check'. That property is false in a reachable state the spec never names. engine.ResolveWorkflow returns the project-config workflow — including its checks — with an empty task-file source when no task file resolves for the spec (internal/engine/workflow_resolve.go:48), and runMechanicalChecks returns an empty result set with allPass=true whenever taskFilePath is empty (internal/cli/review_status.go:174-176). So with checks registered in .tp/config.json and no <base>.tasks.json for the spec (a spec reviewed before tp init), every valid entry mechanizes its class — the candidate is withheld, the register-a-check hint is dropped, next_action stops naming it, and reviewers are told to stop reporting it — while no check ever executes, mechanical_checks is empty, and the exit code is not gated. §3.1's own justification ('An entry tp will never run is not evidence that the class is mechanically checked') points the opposite way from its rule, so the implementer must invent which applies.

finding: The derivability paragraph says `other_roles_open` equals the latest round's total non-PASS count "but only while `spec-coverage` is itself clean in that round, which is what condition 4 guarantees rather than condition 1". For any effective `audit_clean_rounds` >= 1, condition 1 alone forces `spec_coverage_clean_rounds` >= 1, which by §2.2's own equivalence (`open == 0` and `consecutive_clean >= 1` are the same condition) means `spec-coverage` is clean in the latest round — so condition 1 does guarantee it in every configuration except the resolved-0 one. And in that exception it is not condition 4 alone: condition 3 is what makes `engine.Converged` (ConsecutiveClean >= 0 && !StateStale, reviewstate.go:332) reduce to true at a threshold of 0, and only then does condition 4 fail. The sentence attributes a guarantee to one condition that is carried by condition 1 in general and by conditions 3+4 jointly in the corner case, which misdescribes the spec's own conditions to any reader deriving the invariant.

finding: Test 9's second precondition names the wrong set of rounds. It requires that "the rounds above it" carry the same stored roles_hash, but what causes 1-3 actually need is that the *target* round also carries the latest round's stored hash: §2.1 evaluates the hash comparison first, so a target round whose own stored hash differs emits the corpus wording instead of the missing-file, empty-file or unparseable-rows wording — precisely the configuration test 11 constructs on purpose. A fixture that satisfies both preconditions exactly as written can therefore still emit the wrong advisory, which makes the test's own failure claim ("or the walk never reaches it and a correct implementation fails") untrue for a correct implementation.
